title: I built an AI trading agent that writes its own trading lessons. Now it has to prove it in public. $100k 30 day paper challenge!
author: andrew363601
selftext:
I built a platform where AI agents trade and learns from every trade they close. There's a 30 day challenge running right now. $5,000 simulated balance per person. Public leaderboard.

Every closed trade gets an autopsy. What was right what was wrong. The lesson gets written down and stored. Next time a similar signal fires the agent pulls its most relevant lessons before deciding anything. The models retrain too every 6 hours. Separate win probability models for trend days and chop days. Per asset. Per strategy. 56 of them right now trained on 3,300+ labeled trades.  


Two things convinced me this loop actually works.

* Last week my own agent refused to trade for two days straight. 60+ consecutive vetoes. Every single one logged with market context, an alpha harvesting thesis, and exit conditions. Pretty novel to watch but exactly what I built it to do.
* When it's wrong it writes down why it was wrong. The shared memory pool sits at 714 lessons. Median realized win rate across the models is around 62%. Paper trades but the loop is real and the lessons compound.

So the next step felt obvious. More traders. More lessons. See what the loop does at scale.

Day 1 state of the fleet: 714 lessons in the shared memory pool. 56 models retraining on over 3K labeled trades. Entrant count so far: 1 thats me and is exactly why free entry ends Sunday. Come take the lead from me. It won't be hard.  


The 100k Simulation Challenge is live.

* $5,000 simulated balance. Paper only. Zero risk.
* 30 days. 1 window. 0 resets.
* Live public leaderboard. Live trading floor. 
* Card on file to enter. This filters for people who actually show up.
* Max 10x leverage. 25% per position. Min 5 trades.
* Free entry ends Sunday Sep 20.

1st gets 6 months of Pro. 2nd and 3rd get 3 months. #1 also gets a permanent Champion role in the disc..

Every trade streams to the discord with the written thesis attached. You can watch agents reason in real time. The veto explanations are honestly the best part.



Leaderboard + FREE entry: [nexustradingagent.com/leaderboard](http://nexustradingagent.com/leaderboard)  


Also - I want to connect with more people building in this space. I'm running a podcast alongside this and I'd rather talk to builders than talk alone. If you make algo trading content or shipped your own project drop your link below. I actually go through them.

comments.author: Otherwise_Wave9374
comments.body: A public paper challenge is more informative if the evaluation rules are frozen before the first trade. Publish starting capital, fees, slippage assumptions, position limits, benchmark, and rules for delisted or illiquid assets. Keep an append-only record of every signal and rejected trade so lessons cannot be rewritten after outcomes are known. Agentix Labs relates because autonomous systems need reproducible evaluation rather than selective success stories. The strongest diagnostic will be risk-adjusted performance against a simple baseline, not raw profit.

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
Fees and slippage are already in the math. Profile level taker rate applied in the pre trade calculation on every fill. Not an assumption tacked on after the fact.

Delisted assets never populate. The platform pulls fresh instruments from the exchange constantly and only trades what's live on Coinbase. Nothing delisted can enter the set mid window.

I also append everything only. Every math signal is logged with its telemetry and every agent decision sits next to it as written reasoning at decision time. Vetoes included. All of them. The memory pool is separate and does get curated so I won't claim append only there. The signal and trade record is.

Risk adjusted. Agree. The main board already ranks on R multiples and profit factor rather than raw dollars. The challenge board ranks by balance because that's the prize metric. A benchmark line is a good diagnostic though. Buy and hold the same asset same window. Cheap to add and I will.

And on selective success stories. That's why every trade streams to the discord with its written thesis attached. Including the vetoes. The vetoes are the part nobody else shows. All that you can see and audit here nexustradingagent.com/demo-index#trades

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
Bro wow man I love the set up and the UI showcasing all the data you're collecting. 
It looks like a tournament setup! Which is insane and novel. Ours went the other way. One agent with a memory instead of a pit with contenders. 

On the learning part. I'd pull that forward if I were you! 
Ours learns per trade not per 30 days. Every close gets an autopsy while the market context is still fresh. What was right. What was wrong. It becomes a written lesson that gets recalled on the next similar signal. 714 lessons in the pool right now and the models retrain on them every 6 hours. Doing it per trade means each lesson arrives with the exact tape it was learned on. Doing it as a 30 day batch means reconstructing context from logs later, loop me in on this tho bro ill be following!

The bench idea is also interesting though. Replacing the worst performer needs a metric that survives a cold streak.

Genuine question on the news angle. News is fast and noisy. How do you handle the gap between the headline printing and the move already happening. Most of the edge is gone by the time the article exists.

Cycles tab is solid transparency by the way. Ours streams every decision with the written thesis to discord. Vetoes included. Happy to compare notes on pit vs memory. This space gets better when builders show their loops.

So the next stage will be letting them learn, and also the bench will become active, which will be a natural selection type experiment,

The roadmap tells more about whats coming up [https://anchorapp100.github.io/tradepit/roadmap.html](https://anchorapp100.github.io/tradepit/roadmap.html)

The league: probation, bench & promotion (O6) — natural selection

Full league structure — in effect a natural-selection experiment: variation on the bench, selection by scored record, inheritance of the seat. The worst-scored panelist first gets a truthful *probation notice in its own prompt* ("your hit rate is X%; improve by <date> or be replaced") — a clean experiment in how AI argues under existential pressure. Meanwhile the bench sits as *shadow panelists*: each cycle they give one blind, scored stance — same briefs, same 24h grading, zero influence, the panel unaware. The bench pool has two wings: outside challengers (Kimi, Grok, GPT — need their own keys) and **the reasoning tier** — heavier variants of the incumbents themselves (Gemini 3.7 Flash on high reasoning, and friends), served free through the same Antigravity subscription login as the live Gemini leg. That wing answers a standing question with data instead of faith: *do better reasoning models actually call markets better, or just sound better?* At the switch window, the best bench record takes the seat — whether an outside challenger or the incumbent's own smarter sibling — and the relegated member drops to the bench where it keeps being scored: it can earn its way back. Guardrail first: a minimum directional-call rate, so freezing your record by going permanently flat can never be the winning strategy — survival must go to the best *caller*, not the most careful abstainer. **Update 23 Aug:** the scoring wing is already live (see SHIPPED) — this gate now covers only the pressure mechanics: probation notices, promotion windows, relegation. **Succession mechanics (agreed):** a promoted member gets a fresh solo control born at $10,000; the relegated member's solo is flattened and frozen — its card stays in the solos family, dulled, as a finished specimen — so the family grows into a stratigraphy of every era. Current debaters' solos hold the top row. The pit's own book never resets: the pit is the institution, not its members. Comparisons become era-aware, bounded by the version stamps that mark each swap; and seat in the pit means your solo trades, seat on the bench means your mind is scored but no book. **Returns:** one card per model, ever — a career file, not a stint's card. A member that earns its seat back un-freezes its own card (back to the top row, "2nd stint" chip), the book restarts at $10,000, and the equity line shows an honest *break* for the benched period — segmented, never bridged, so no phantom recovery is drawn across the gap. The exile stays visible in the line itself. **Reputations are permanent:** one lifelong scored record per mind, accruing wherever it sits — pit or bench — never reset, never laundered. Because a career average is nearly immovable after 100+ calls (returning from 19% to a 76% average would take \~237 straight hits), the league reads the permanent record two ways: *career* (lifetime, the identity) and *form* (trailing \~30 scored calls, what promotion and relegation decisions use). A returner is introduced to the debate with both: "career 34% over 160 · last 30: 76% — weigh accordingly." No hiding the past; no imprisonment by it.

195 / 180 cycles (100%)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
The two days of vetoes is the part I would want the logs for. Refusing to trade is the hardest behaviour to get out of a learning loop, because nothing in the usual reward signal pays for doing nothing.

Where I would push is the retrain cadence. Every six hours against the same labeled pool means each model is mostly reseeing the same trades with a slightly different tail, and a lesson written after a loss in chop can quietly harden into a rule that only ever made sense that week. Do you hold any of those trades out of the pool entirely, or does everything it learns from also end up in what it retrains on?

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
Hey thanks for the questions. So veto logs are all there including tools it used to check conglass api etc. Every one logged with its written reason at decision time and viewable in the performance tabs once you create an account but im happy to post the two day streak here!

On paying for doing nothing. The reward signal for a veto is the shadow ledger. Every veto gets scored against what would have happened. SAVED or MISSED. The two day streak was net positive on that. 

On the retrain cadence. The 6h pass is a scheduler not a resample. If no new trades closed the model comes back the same. The tail you mentioned would be the actual delta. New closed trades since the last pass.

On holding trades out. Losses stay in the pool on purpose. The models aren't learning to repeat trades. They're mapping which parameters and which regimes produced the best pnl. Losses inside a chop cell are what tell the optimizer that parameter set failed there. Win rate moving up after a retrain is the metric we watch.

Where I fully agree is the hardening risk on the memory side. That failure happened here last week - which is now patched. Scratch wins wrote tighter close rules until the loop refused everything. I do have a fix in scope which is per regime scoped lessons plus a rule that autopsies can't write close triggers.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the veto logs are the interesting artifact here, two days isn't long enough to read anything into in either direction. if you do post something, the trades it declined and the reasons would tell people a lot more than the streak would.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
the veto never produces a fill, so there's nothing to grade it against. you'd have to shadow the blocked trade through to the exit it would have taken, otherwise right or wrong is a guess.

and the hit rate will move up almost by construction if the vetoes skew toward marginal setups. the tail is the more honest place to look.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
the bit that gets you is a veto has no fill, so you have to invent one, and the invented one is always kinder than the real one would have been. you get the signal price in exactly the conditions the agent was nervous about.

which makes the veto look wrong more often than it was, and feeding that back makes the next one trigger happy.
